issues.description: Constructor parameter order for Meal is inconsistent between the problem specification / solution and the template. The UML and the solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template's Meal class defines the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This will cause compilation errors in example code (Main) and confuse students about the intended constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template Meal constructor with the UML and solution by changing its signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and updating parameter usage accordingly. This ensures example code in Main compiles and matches the exercise specification.

issues.description: The Meal constructor parameter order differs across artifacts: the problem statement UML and the solution define Meal(String, String[]) (name first, then ingredients), but the template implementation declares the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (ingredients first). The Main example in the problem/comments also uses the (String, String[]) order. This inconsistency will confuse students when instantiating Meal and when mapping the problem requirements to the provided template code and expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor signature to match the problem statement and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and update the parameter assignments accordingly so the name is the first parameter and ingredients the second.
